h: A Belvedere, a Castle and the Coast
p: Haldon Hill has a landmark worth seeking out: Haldon Belvedere, also known as Lawrence Castle, a striking triangular tower built in the eighteenth century and visible for miles around. It's a short drive from the forest park and adds a quirky bit of history to an outdoorsy day.

Head down off the ridge towards the estuary and you'll find Powderham Castle, the historic home of the Earls of Devon, with a deer park sitting right beside the River Exe. From there, it's not far to the seaside at Dawlish and Dawlish Warren, where the railway famously runs along the sea wall and the sandy spit is great for a breezy walk.

For your Go Ape session, set aside a couple of hours and arrive with a bit of time in hand. The forest is a popular spot with walkers and bikers, and you'll want a relaxed start rather than a sprint from the car. Wear layers, because exposed bits of the ridge can feel cooler and windier than the city below.

If you're staying in Exeter, Dartmoor is also within easy reach, so a Haldon morning can kick off a bigger Devon trip. Between moorland, coast and countryside, this corner of the county has a cracking mix for active families who like variety.
